request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a contact, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does**
- **Storing it:** the contact is trimmed and lower-cased before it is saved. A blank contact means none, and the row shows it empty.
- **Duplicates:** a contact another person on the sheet already has is refused before anything is written. The form shows its error (`person-form-error`), nothing is saved and nothing goes to the audit file. A person can keep their own contact when they are edited.
- **Audit:**
  - `PERSON_ADDED` gets ` contact=<contact>` at the end only when the form gave one.
  - `PERSON_EDITED` gets it at the end only when the contact differs from the stored one. If it was cleared, the line ends in `contact=` with nothing after it.

**Changes**
- **Database:** new migration `V51__person_contact.sql` adds a nullable `contact` column to `person`.
- **Server:**
  - `Person` and `PersonRequest` carry the contact.
  - `ValidatePerson` trims and lower-cases it.
  - `People` reads and writes it, and has a new `contactTaken` check.
  - `BuildPerson` and `SavePerson` refuse a duplicate and write the audit fields.
  - The bulk grade action keeps each person's current contact, so it never changes or audits one.
- **Front end:** the person form has a contact input (`person-form-contact`), the row shows it (`person-contact`), the editor fills it in when opened, and the error message now mentions contacts.

Duplicates are checked in the app, not by a unique index in the database. I did that so any other code that copies people between sheets can't start failing on a database constraint. The downside is that two saves at exactly the same moment could, in theory, both get the same contact through.
